subject: ACME sidecar pattern for cert delegation on private hosts
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: forrest.jensen@edgeops.io, security@acme-biomed.com
Cc: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME sidecar pattern for cert delegation on private hosts

Forrest / Acme Security team,

Following our call this morning, I wanted to capture a lightweight proposal for certificate management in private deployments where customers own their DNS (private Route 53 or on-prem BIND) and we want to avoid manual cert handoffs every time a host is provisioned. High level idea: run an ACME-capable sidecar (or small agent) co-located with the Redwood private runtime that requests short-lived leaf certs from a customer-controlled ACME CA (or an intermediary we operate) using a delegated validation record. Rationale:

- Minimizes long-lived private keys on Redwood side.
- Lets customers retain control of the issuing CA policy.
- Short-lived certs reduce blast radius for host compromise.

Key components: 
- DNS delegation: a CNAME or TXT delegation zone that the customer points for *.redwood.private.example -> _acme.redwood.example (private zone)
- Sidecar ACME client: runs cert rotation (default 24h TTL for leaf certs, renew at 16h), stores certs in memory with local mTLS to the runtime proxy (Envoy).
- Local TLS termination vs edge proxy: prefer Envoy sidecar terminate mTLS locally and forward over loopback to the process to avoid exposing private keys.

Constraints & edge cases:
- Air-gapped customers: offline signing path required (we can produce CSR and ship for an offline CA signature)
- CNAMEs are ideal for cloud-hosted private zones; legacy BIND admins often require adding TXT records for validation which requires ops coordination
- Auditing: sidecar must emit cert events to the private control plane log endpoint (signed audit entries)

Attached is a diagram and a short checklist for rollout. Could you confirm whether Acme BioMed is comfortable with CNAME delegation in their private zone, or if they want an explicit TXT-based validation flow?

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Forrest Jensen <forrest.jensen@edgeops.io>
To: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, security@acme-biomed.com
Date: 2027-06-20T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME sidecar pattern for cert delegation on private hosts

Chloe,

Thanks for writing this up. EdgeOps has implemented a very similar pattern for internal services — we call it the "ACME sidecar proxy". Quick notes from our side based on your checklist:

- CNAME delegation is the fastest for our customers on private clouds. It works well if they allow the delegation of a narrow subdomain (_acme.example.internal).
- For on-prem BIND admins we often provide an automation script that creates a one-time validation TXT and then removes it post-issue. That reduces human ops work.
- Short-lived certs (12–24h) are fine; watch for clock skew on older Windows hosts.

Operationally, two recommendations:
1) Tokenized challenge: issue a one-time validation token with a 1h TTL that the sidecar can present to the customer zone via an API the customer runs (preferred for strict environments).
2) Graceful failure mode: sidecar should start serving using a pre-provisioned fallback cert from the customer (longer lifetime) if ACME fails for >30 minutes and surface a clear alert to the control plane.

I'm attaching a short ops runbook (PDF) that outlines the playbook we used for 10 customers. Happy to hop on a call with Acme's infra team.

—Forrest
Forrest Jensen
Solutions Architect, EdgeOps
From: security@acme-biomed.com <security@acme-biomed.com>

Date: 2027-06-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME sidecar pattern for cert delegation on private hosts

Chloe / Forrest / team,

We reviewed the proposal with our platform & security leads. High-level reactions:

- We prefer a model where Acme BioMed retains signing authority. An intermediary CA operated by Redwood is acceptable only if we can require:
  * Short-lived leaf certs (<= 24h)
  * Full transparency of issuance logs (we need RFC-compliant OCSP/CT-style records or signed issuance events delivered to our audit endpoint)
- CNAME delegation is acceptable if scoped tightly to a single subdomain and if rollback is trivial. Our BIND team will not accept automated TXT insertion scripts without prior approval.
- Air-gapped sites: we need an offline signing workflow with an HSM-backed signatory and signed audit bundle returned over an approved transfer process.

Please update the runbook to include: CSR generation details, exact audit event schema, and the offline signing checklist. Also include a rollback procedure that removes the delegation and rotates previously issued tokens.

Security will schedule a short technical review next week; please provide the updated artifacts by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Acme Security Team
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: security@acme-biomed.com, forrest.jensen@edgeops.io
Cc: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-23T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME sidecar pattern for cert delegation on private hosts — updated artifacts

Thanks for the feedback — summarized next steps and the attached deliverables:

1) Updated runbook (sidecar-acme-checklist.pdf) including:
   - CSR/CSR-sanitization steps we use before sending to any signing authority
   - Audit event schema: {event_id, issued_at, subject, issuer_fingerprint, sidecar_id, signed_by} (we'll deliver as signed JSON lines to your audit endpoint)
   - Offline signing flow: csr -> signed bundle, HSM signature requirement, transfer checklist

2) Implementation notes for the sidecar:
   - Default rotation: attempt renewal at 16h, fallback to pre-provisioned cert after 30m failed attempts.
   - Local storage: memory-only by default; optional encrypted disk if customer allows.
   - Envoy integration: TLS Context hot-reload on cert replace, health check that disables route if cert unavailable.

3) Rollback/playbook:
   - Remove CNAME/TXT delegation and publish a short-lived revocation marker in the delegated zone so sidecars stop attempting ACME validation for 1h.
   - Re-issue any required long-lived fallback certs.

Action items:
- Dev (Dev Patel): create a small proof-of-concept sidecar binary and a minimal public API that accepts a CSR and writes audit events to an S3-compatible endpoint. Target: 2-week spike.
- Infra (Karthik): prepare a checklist for BIND teams at target customers that explains the manual TXT process and rollback steps.
- Ops (Marissa): schedule a 30-minute technical review with Acme BioMed for 2027-06-28 10:00 PT.

I've uploaded the diagram and runbook to the linked Drive folder. Forrest — can you share the EdgeOps runbook you mentioned so we can merge best practices?

Chloe
Chloe Martin
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
